title: Sri Aurobindo Ashram Delhi - History, Timings, Meditation & Travel Guide
content:
Sri Aurobindo Ashram - Delhi,

Amid Delhi’s busy streets, Sri Aurobindo Ashram (often called Arbindo Ashram) is a calm retreat for those seeking peace, meditation, and spiritual learning. With its quiet gardens, meditation halls, and teachings of Sri Aurobindo and The Mother, the ashram has become a favorite destination for both spiritual seekers and travelers who want to escape the chaos of city life.

History & Significance:

The Sri Aurobindo Ashram Delhi, also known as the Arbindo Ashram, was established in 1956 to spread the teachings of Sri Aurobindo and The Mother (Mirra Alfassa) in the capital city. While the main ashram is in Pondicherry, the Delhi branch was created to bring their message of peace, spirituality, and Integral Yoga closer to people in North India.

Sri Aurobindo (1872–1950) was not only a philosopher and yogi but also a freedom fighter, poet, and thinker who played a key role in India’s independence movement before dedicating his life to spiritual practice. His spiritual partner, The Mother, continued his vision and developed the concept of Integral Yoga—a path that seeks harmony between mind, body, and spirit while living an active life in society.

The Delhi Ashram is more than just a place for meditation. It has become a cultural and spiritual hub, where people attend meditation sessions, yoga workshops, and talks on philosophy and life. The ashram also houses a library and bookstore with works of Sri Aurobindo and The Mother, making it a center for deep learning and reflection.

Over the decades, the ashram has grown into a peaceful retreat in the heart of Delhi, where visitors from India and abroad come to experience inner calm, away from the noise of the city. Its simple yet meaningful atmosphere carries forward the legacy of Sri Aurobindo’s vision of a life that unites spiritual practice with everyday living.

Things to Do at Aurobindo Ashram:

  • Meditation & Yoga – Join guided sessions for peace and self-awareness.
  • Visit the Library & Bookstore – Read or buy works by Sri Aurobindo and The Mother.
  • Stroll in the Gardens – Perfect for reflection and relaxation.
  • Attend Workshops & Programs – Learn about yoga, spirituality, and cultural activities.
  • Connect with Community – Experience simple, meaningful living with like-minded seekers.

Best Time to Visit: The ashram welcomes visitors all year. However, the best time to visit is from October to March, when Delhi’s weather is pleasant for walking and meditation. Early mornings and evenings are especially peaceful.

How to Reach:

  • Nearest Metro Station: INA Metro Station (Yellow & Pink Line) – about 1 km away.
  • By Road: Well connected by autos, cabs, and buses from anywhere in Delhi.
  • Parking Information: Limited parking is available nearby public transport is more convenient.

Timings:

  • Morning: 8:00 AM – 12:00 PM and Evening: 2:00 PM – 6:00 PM.
  • Closed on: Major public holidays and special occasions (check before visiting).

Nearby Attractions:

  • Lodhi Gardens - A green historical park (2 km away).
  • Dilli Haat (INA) - Popular for food and crafts.
  • India Habitat Centre -  A cultural hub with exhibitions and events.
  • Safdarjung Tomb - A beautiful Mughal monument close to the ashram.

Travel Tips: Keep silence inside meditation areas, Wear modest and comfortable clothes, Mobile phones should be on silent mode, Some workshops require advance registration.
excerpt: Sri Aurobindo Ashram Delhi is more than just a meditation center – it’s a place where one can find peace, learn yoga, and explore the spiritual vision of Sri Aurobindo and The Mother. With its calm gardens, meditation halls, and library, it offers visitors a much-needed break from Delhi’s fast-paced lifestyle.
